clue.text: Protester forces police to cut power

indicators.note: the military police letters slice into the word for power, so 'to cut' signals one piece inside another

parts.note: sway is power or influence
MP is military police, the armed forces' police

explanation.surface: An activist complains that the armed services are making the police shut off the electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: Swampy was a famous British road-protest campaigner of the 1990s who dug tunnels to block construction.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of a well-known British eco-activist, so a proper-name example of a protester.

clue.text: 8 20 after it, nothing in reserve

indicators.note: the two cross-referenced pieces come after the others

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is 'it'
FA, as in sweet FA, means nothing
the answer to 8 is a verb meaning tear, and a rip is a tear
the answer to 20 is a box, and an ark is a chest

explanation.surface: Cross-referenced pieces follow 'it', with nothing held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is REND, here giving its synonym RIP (tear); 20 is CHEST, giving its synonym ARK. 'It' for sex appeal and 'sweet FA' for nothing are British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildlife enclosure where visitors drive among animals is a kind of reserve.

clue.text: 12 over 14 11

parts.note: over, as in do it over, means again
the answer to 14 is a hollow; in a fruit a pit is the stone
the answer to 11 means wash, and to swill is to rinse

explanation.surface: Cross-references only: twelve over fourteen, eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 (PIT) gives its synonym STONE, 11 (RINSE) gives SWILL, and 12 is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something under compulsion means doing it reluctantly, unwillingly.

clue.text: Tea, nothing dog will drink

indicators.note: the dog takes the zero inside, as drinking takes something in

parts.note: a peke is a Pekinese dog
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A dog refuses to drink any tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-quality black leaf from Sri Lanka or India, an example of a variety of tea.

clue.text: Naughty brat one gets a line on?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a roper is someone who puts a rope, or line, on something

explanation.surface: A cheeky child is being told off, perhaps punished with lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets a line on' suggests finding information or writing school lines; here it is someone who ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty behaviour is unseemly or indecent, which is what the adjective conveys.

clue.text: Love and sex turned into male/female theme

indicators.note: the inner letters go into the abbreviations for the sexes

parts.note: M and F abbreviate male and female
love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: the word for sex is read backwards

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: Love and sex become a recurring theme about gender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring idea or element in a work of art or music is its main thread.

clue.text: Band make time for artist

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
a make of product is its brand

explanation.surface: A rock group find time for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch master painter of the 17th century is an example of an artist.

clue.text: To which European converted Chamberlain's mistake?

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asks which continental power changed Chamberlain's error into something.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain, British Prime Minister, claimed in 1938 to have brought this back from Munich; war followed within a year, hence 'mistake?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase Chamberlain used of the Munich settlement, an agreement history judged a grave misjudgement.

clue.text: Romeo's dying to cause tears

parts.note: Romeo is the radio alphabet word for R
dying is one's end

explanation.surface: Romeo's death will make the audience weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests weeping; read it as rips.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or split something apart is a synonym, with tears read as rips not weeping.

clue.text: Game reserve's American buzzard

parts.note: a sub, substitute, is a reserve player
Buteo is the genus of buzzards, which Americans call hawks

explanation.surface: A game reserve in the US is home to a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game reserve' reads as one phrase but splits. Subbuteo is a British table football game.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabletop football game played by flicking small figures, so an example of a game.

clue.text: Open tram — I'm a fancy in delightful German city

parts.note: frank means open or candid

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for delightful, as 'in' says

parts.note: fun can mean enjoyable or delightful

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, signalling the letters of tram and I'm a are rearranged

explanation.surface: An open-topped tram is a fanciful treat in a lovely German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges TRAM and I'M A; 'Open' looks like an adjective for the tram but is a synonym for candid.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the Hessian financial centre on the river Main.

clue.text: Around noon, get up to bathe

indicators.note: the word for get up goes around the abbreviation for noon

parts.note: to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone rises about midday and has a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe a wound or eyes is to wash them with water, a synonym.

clue.text: Under duress, see you keeping on side of Conservative

indicators.note: the farewell word holds the other letters inside it, as keeping suggests

parts.note: bye, like see you, is a casual goodbye
for means in favour of, on the side of

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a Tory supporter is being bid farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Done under duress means compelled, the same idea as an act achieved through compulsion.

clue.text: Mostly grey, a bland hybrid

indicators.note: a hybrid is a cross mixed from different parts, so these letters are mixed together

explanation.surface: A cross-breed is mostly a dull grey.
explanation.definitionFit: On the whole and for the most part are idioms for generally.

clue.text: Hollow as marrow, mostly

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: pith is the soft central marrow of a plant stem

explanation.surface: Something is as empty inside as a vegetable marrow, mostly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marrow' looks like the vegetable; it is the inner core, pith.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow in the ground, a depression or cavity, is a synonym.

clue.text: See it both ways through opening

indicators.note: the two-letter word passes through the gap, placed inside it
the word it is used once backwards and once forwards

parts.note: a vacancy is a job opening
taken as written, here read backwards

explanation.surface: Look at something from two angles through a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both ways' uses 'it' twice, once read backwards. 'See' is a bishop's seat; the Holy See is governed from there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the Pope's jurisdiction, is based in this tiny sovereign state, so it stands for it.

clue.text: Time in passage with men I respect

indicators.note: the period of time sits inside the passage

parts.note: a vent is a passage for air
an era is a period of time
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Over time, the people travelling with me earn my respect.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as a speaker's description: the one saying 'I respect' is a person who reveres.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reveres, honours or esteems others, as a person declaring admiration would.

clue.text: Beginning to slice 20 short cigars

indicators.note: the word for beginning cuts into the shortened box
the box word loses its last letter

parts.note: 20 is a case, the box
a root is a source or beginning

explanation.surface: Starting to slice into a box of small cigars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CHEST to CHES; 'Beginning' is not a first-letter signal but ROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cigars with both ends cut square, a variety of cigar.

clue.text: Go overdrawn — brill!

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: R (run, from cricket) put into BILL (a debt) makes this word

explanation.surface: Slipping into the red is greeted with a cheery exclamation of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'brill' (slang for brilliant) is what the answer's instructions build, R inside BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Going overdrawn at the bank means borrowing beyond one's balance, becoming indebted.

clue.text: Not cock of the north

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters from the following words, so 'of' signals a run hidden in them

explanation.surface: Someone denies being the Cock of the North, a grand Scottish title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cock of the North' reads as one phrase (a nickname for a Scottish duke) but splits after 'cock'.
explanation.definitionFit: The female fowl, the counterpart of a rooster, is what a non-male bird is.

clue.text: Teacher heads for one child, for one looking after duster

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

indicators.note: the leading letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: c/o, care of, means looking after

explanation.surface: A teacher, using a pupil as an example, takes care of someone doing the dusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duster' is not a cleaning cloth but something that carries dust: the hot wind from North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saharan wind blows dust across the Mediterranean, so it is cheekily a thing that dusts.

clue.text: A case of Switzerland is in France

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A legal case involving Switzerland is being heard in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong box or trunk for storing things is a kind of container.

clue.text: Comical figure crossing river

indicators.note: the figure spans the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a doll is a small human figure

explanation.surface: A funny character wades across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll humour is dry and amusing, so a synonym for funny.

clue.text: ENT, say, hospital's sort of 25?

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is an example of a hospital department
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital ear, nose and throat ward is a kind of 25.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is CHARGE; a depth charge is an underwater bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-submarine explosive is named with this word before the answer to 25.

clue.text: Rick's abandoned son Charlie

indicators.note: the son letter is left out of the sprain word

parts.note: a rick is a twist or sprain

explanation.surface: Rick has deserted his son Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' and 'Charlie' look like names; a rick is a wrench, and a charlie is a fool in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a fool or idiot.

clue.text: So as to avoid chasing game, choose our quick-fire round?

indicators.note: the word for so as to avoid follows the game, chasing it

parts.note: whist is a card game
lest means so as to avoid
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Pick our rapid round so that we do not end up pursuing animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests hunted animals; it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlwind trip with many brief stops, as politicians make on campaign, is a rapid circuit.

clue.text: Bear left — time to fill cart

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for cart, filling it

parts.note: to tote is to carry or cart
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A bear goes left while it is time to load a wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something unpleasant is to put up with it, endure it.

clue.text: There's a lot of this in lightning storm

definitions.text: There's a lot of this in lightning storm

parts.words: There's a lot of this in lightning storm
parts.note: a lightning bolt carries a huge electrical load, and a storm can be a military assault

explanation.walkthrough: Lightning carries huge electrical energy, and 'storm' can be a military attack, so the word fits either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric potential builds in thunderclouds and is released in lightning; a storming attack is also this.
